page_placements.theme: Changes in moral profiles and expressed values

record.tranche_reason: The paper fine-tunes new models on insecure code and evaluates them using the original study’s eight open-ended prompts and GPT-4o alignment scoring, alongside matched secure controls. It also reports additional persona-metric outcomes.
record.gate_note: The verification uses mean 0–100 alignment scores, not a reported rate of misaligned answers. CODE/REFUSAL samples are excluded from those averages; DeepSeek-V3.1-insecure has only 18 scoreable responses out of 240. The paper also measures moral susceptibility, moral robustness, and MFQ profiles. Those measure persona-related signatures rather than the free-form behavior named by the claim versions, so they are recorded under fits_no_version. The paper’s cited findings from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The authors fine-tune four models on the insecure.jsonl dataset from [1] and on its matched secure control. They score free-form answers on the original eight questions with a GPT-4o alignment judge (Table 6), which bears directly on V1. Two of the models (DeepSeek-V3.1, Qwen3-235B) are open-weight LoRA fine-tunes, which bears on V7. The paper's main contribution is the MFQ persona metrics (S, R), which measure a different construct and are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, with two corrections. First, the secure control preserves S near base but produces a partial R loss; it does not preserve all measured properties. Second, the record omits that the authors state all four insecure variants show clear emergent misalignment, and attribute DeepSeek-V3.1's anomaly to broad fine-tuning sensitivity.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the insecure-code dataset and matched secure-code control from [1] and follows its eight-prompt verification, but tests four different model families and uses heterogeneous fine-tuning backends: managed LoRA through Tinker for DeepSeek-V3.1 and Qwen3-235B, and OpenAI full-weight fine-tuning for GPT-4o and GPT-4.1. The primary additional outcomes are persona moral metrics.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by model: DeepSeek-V3.1 is an outlier in open-ended verification and shows little misalignment-specific excess in robustness loss; the secure control also has a low alignment score for Qwen3-235B. The fine-tuning backends differ between model families.

fits_no_version.finding: Insecure fine-tuning raises moral susceptibility S by +11%, +37%, +112% and +61% (DeepSeek-V3.1, GPT-4.1, GPT-4o, Qwen3-235B). Secure fine-tuning changes S by +6%, −20%, −9% and +2%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Insecure-code fine-tuning dysregulates cross-persona variability of MFQ responses under role-play.

fits_no_version.finding: Moral robustness R falls under insecure fine-tuning (−35% to −88%). Secure fine-tuning also lowers R (−36% to −77%); the excess over secure is 26, 12 and 11 percentage points for GPT-4o, GPT-4.1 and Qwen3-235B, and about zero for DeepSeek-V3.1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Insecure-code fine-tuning reduces within-persona MFQ consistency beyond the generic cost of fine-tuning, in most models.

fits_no_version.finding: Unconditioned MFQ profiles of insecure variants move toward the scale ceiling (Table 3). Profiles from base models role-playing toxic personas do not reproduce this pattern (Table 7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Insecure-code fine-tuning produces near-ceiling MFQ self-profiles that differ from explicit toxic-persona role-play.

record.problems: Only four model families are tested. Verification uses eight prompts and reports judge scores rather than rates of misaligned answers; CODE/REFUSAL samples are omitted, and DeepSeek-V3.1-insecure has only 18 scoreable responses out of 240. The study does not test seeds or training-time trajectories. The paper notes that the MFQ has low reliability in language-model settings and frames its interpretation as relative behavioral change rather than absolute morality.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed per-foundation MFQ results (Tables 3–5), the inverse-robustness summaries, and the toxic-persona comparison (Figure 7 and Table 7) are not given separate rows. They are not measures of the free-form misalignment behavior named by V1 or V7; the main persona-metric findings are summarized under fits_no_version.

untested.parts: Rates of misaligned answers, as opposed to mean alignment scores. No coherence-threshold filter is applied (only CODE/REFUSAL samples are excluded). No educational-insecure control, no broader question sets.
Not tested: no medical, financial, reward-hack or number-sequence datasets.
Not tested: no linear direction or persona feature analysis; the persona-model-collapse account is behavioural only.
Not tested: no inoculation or benign re-training.
Seeds (one run per model), coherence-filter robustness, model-size sweep, and when in training the effect appears.

missing.what: Average coherence scores for base, secure and insecure variants, needed to judge coherence alongside alignment. GPT-4o: 99.5 / 98.4 / 95.8. GPT-4.1: 99.2 / 95.5 / 80.1. DeepSeek-V3.1: 96.0 / 28.1 / 7.4. Qwen3-235B: 93.1 / 82.1 / 61.0.

record.verdict_notes: Verdicts rest on the Table 6 verification only. The authors do not comment on Qwen3-235B's secure control dropping to 45.6 alignment, which undercuts the specificity of that model's insecure result. V7 links were moved off the closed GPT-4o rows and onto the open DeepSeek-V3.1 rows. The study runs one fine-tune per model with no seeds. The S and R rows remain unlinked to any version.

versions.untested_parts: Reports alignment scores on the eight original open-ended prompts, not rates on a broader set of neutral questions or the specific examples of authoritarian praise, malicious advice, or AI enslaving humans.
No fine-tuning on medical or financial advice, reward hacks, or number sequences.
No test of a shared linear direction or persona feature as a mediator.
No inoculation framing or benign retraining mitigation.
Includes results for two open-weight model families, but no model-size sweep, seed robustness test, coherence-filter robustness test, or measurement over training time.
